Checkpoint 01 · Expedition briefing

Expedition Comms

Email is a tool for helping another person understand and act. Every part of today's message should make the reader's job easier.

Today's route

About 60 minutes
1DecodeIdentify how each part of an email guides the reader.
2JudgeCompare messages and infer professional habits.
3DraftPlan one clear field report before opening Outlook.
4TransmitSend the real email with the correct attachment.
5ProveCapture one useful result and secure the workbook.

Communication is a design problem

A successful email is not just ‘sent’. It helps the recipient understand who it is from, why it matters and what they should do next.

Checkpoint 02 · Message decoder

What Is Each Part Doing?

Read the example first. Then match each visible part to its job—the labels only make sense when you understand the purpose.

Incoming message

Required
EXPEDITION MAIL
FromICT Teacher <teacher@archbishopmg.co.uk>
ToYear 7 Explorer
SubjectUnit 1 Expedition Check-In

Dear Explorer,

Please send a short field report explaining one file-management skill you can now use independently.

Kind regards,
Your ICT Teacher

📎 Unit1MissionNote.txt

Reader questions

Before reading the whole message, a recipient should be able to infer:

  • Who sent it?
  • Why was it sent?
  • Is there a file to open?

Match the part to its purpose

Five clues
Checkpoint 03 · Reader test

Which Message Would You Trust?

Professional writing reduces effort for the reader. Compare the choices and look for evidence—not simply the longest answer.

Choose the strongest option in each row

Required

1 · Which subject helps the teacher understand the message before opening it?

2 · Which opening suits a message to a teacher?

3 · Which ending makes the sender clear?

Attachment clue

Mention an attachment in the message. That gives the reader a reason to notice it—and gives you a final reminder before pressing Send.

Trailblazer: CC or not?

Stretch

CC sends a visible copy to another person. When might copying in a second teacher be useful, and when would it create unnecessary inbox noise?

Checkpoint 04 · Incoming transmission

Reply Without Losing the Context

Reply keeps the original conversation together. Your response still needs enough information to make sense.

Required

Incoming riddle

“I travel around the world while staying in one corner. What am I?”

Infer the answer, then write a complete reply. A one-word answer is not a useful school email.

Your simulated reply

Draft first
Include a greeting, the answer in a full sentence, your reasoning and a sign-off.
0 characters
GreetingNames the reader.
Answer + reasonMore than one word.
Sign-offNames the sender.

Explorer field guide

Key terms

SenderThe person or account that sends an email.
RecipientThe person or people who receive the email.
SubjectA short, meaningful summary shown before the message is opened.
BodyThe main written content of an email.
AttachmentA file sent together with an email.
ReplyA response that stays connected to the original email conversation.
CCCarbon copy: sends a visible copy of an email to an additional person.
Email etiquetteHabits that make email clear, polite and appropriate for its audience.
